subject: CareBridge - model fit & benchmarking logistics
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@carebridge.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Discovery and evaluation goals (CareBridge)

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the quick walkthrough of Redwood. To recap from our side:

- Primary goal: baseline an LLM for triage/clinical-note summarization and short-answer extraction (patient-facing notes, ~150-400 tokens).
- Success metrics: answer accuracy on curated QA set, hallucination rate (false statements cited as facts), and average latency at 1–5 qps.
- Dataset: we can share a stratified sample (~1k cases) with de-identified text. Attached is a 1k sample (carebridge-sample-1000.jsonl) with columns we currently have.

Requests / asks:
1) Can Redwood propose 2–3 candidate model variants to evaluate (tradeoffs: cost vs. accuracy)?
2) What exact dataset format and labeling do you need for the benchmark run?
3) Example prompt templates and scorer rubric so our clinical reviewers understand how outputs will be scored.
4) Rough timeline + any permissions we need to grant Redwood to run an evaluation on our data (SFTP, signed upload link, or direct Drive).

Next steps we'd like within this week: model suggestions and a short eval checklist so we can confirm resources and timing.

Thanks,
Jake
Sr. Product Manager
CareBridge Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-07T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery and evaluation goals (CareBridge)

Appreciate the clear summary, Jake — and thanks for sending the sample. High level reply/proposal below; Karthik will add the technical spec for ingest and scoring.

Quick proposal (initial evaluation run):
- Candidate models: Redwood-Std-7B-q4 (lower compute/cost, good for throughput), Redwood-Long-13B-v2 (balanced accuracy for longer context), and Open-Shared-70B-int8 (higher-quality baseline we can fall back to if needed).
- Evaluation mode: batch offline run on your sample + holdout (we recommend 80/20 split) to measure accuracy/hallucination; optionally a streaming latency run for p95 at 1–5 qps.
- Suggested scoring: accuracy (exact/span match) 50%, hallucination rate 30% (binary flag when output contains unsupported clinical assertions), and answer usefulness (clinician-rated 1–5) 20%. We'll provide the rubric for clinician raters.
- Prompt sets: attached is a starter set (carebridge_eval_prompts.md) with instruction templates for summary and extract tasks. Please review and tell us if you want conservative or recall-oriented wording.

Operational asks:
- Please confirm you can share a production-style sample over SFTP or via a signed upload link. If you prefer Drive, share folder perms for redwood-eval@redwood.ai.
- For PII/PHI: we'll treat the dataset per our standard Private deployment handling for evaluation (encrypted at rest, restricted access, and no retention beyond the run unless you opt in). See the SOC2 summary I attached for initial assurance. Karthik will include the audit/log access options.

Suggested timeline:
- Today (Thu): Karthik sends dataset format + scoring spec.
- Fri: CareBridge confirms dataset share method & prompt preferences.
- Next Tue: Redwood runs first pass and shares results + raw outputs and scorer artifacts.

If that works, Ben and I will draft a short MOU for the eval (data handling + duration) and an estimate for a one-off evaluation charge.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales (Model Fit)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@carebridge.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-08T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery and evaluation goals (CareBridge) — dataset & scoring spec

Thanks — attaching a compact spec below. I kept it tight so your engineering team can map quickly. If anything isn't feasible, flag and we'll adjust.

Dataset format (required): JSONL, UTF-8, newline-delimited. Each record should include these top-level fields:
- id (string)
- task ("summary" | "extract")
- input (string) — clinical note text (de-identified)
- reference (string) — the expected answer/summary for scorer comparison (for extract tasks, include the canonical span)
- context_meta (optional) — patient-age, note-type, visit-date (ISO date)

Scoring criteria (automated + clinician review):
- Exact/span-match (automated): 0–1 per item (weight 50%). Use token-level span compare for extract tasks and normalized whitespace/lowercase exact match for short answers.
- Hallucination flag (clinician): binary 0/1 when output asserts unsupported clinical facts (weight 30%). Provide a short justification field for each flagged item.
- Usefulness (clinician): Likert 1–5 normalized to 0–1 (weight 20%).

Outputs we'll produce: raw model outputs (per item), automated scorer CSV, clinician scorer sheet (Google Sheet template) with links to each item, and a final summary report (accuracy, hallucination rate, per-category breakdown).

Run notes & config:
- Sequence length: set max input to 4k tokens; for summarization we recommend chunk+overlap when notes exceed 4k.
- Batching: for the initial run use batch size 8 on Redwood-Std-7B-q4; we can increase for throughput runs.
- Quantization: 4-bit q4 for cost-effective runs; we'll run the 70B-int8 only for the gold baseline and with limited concurrency.

Deliverables and timeline (technical):
- You: confirm dataset upload method + attach a README mapping fields by Fri EOD.
- Redwood: once dataset is received, we’ll validate format within 24 hours and run a full offline pass (~48 hours for 1k sample across three models).

Attached: redwood_eval_spec.json (example spec + scorer config). I'll provision a Google Sheet template in the Drive folder and share with your reviewers.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. Quick clarifications from our security/compliance side before we share the full 1k:
1) PII/PHI handling: Can you confirm no raw identifiers will be stored beyond the evaluation run? What retention window do you enforce for eval datasets?
2) Audit logs: can we get S3-style access logs or a signed report of who accessed the dataset during the run?
3) If we need an on-prem evaluation (air-gapped), do you offer a package for one-off runs?

Also: our clinicians would like to see a sample of the Google Sheet scorer layout before we commit reviewers — can you share the template link?

We can do the upload by Friday if the answers above are straightforward.

Emma
Head of Clinical Ops
CareBridge Health
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@carebridge.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery and evaluation goals (CareBridge) — dataset & scoring spec

Thanks, Emma — quick answers inline and next steps.

1) Retention: We do not retain raw uploaded evaluation datasets beyond 30 days by default; for this one-off eval we can set a 14-day retention window and delete earlier on request. All eval data is encrypted at rest and in transit. See attached redwood_soc2_summary.pdf for our controls; we’ll include a short MOU that documents the retention window you select.

2) Audit logs: yes — we can provide an access log export (S3-compatible) for the run and a signed activity report. We’ll include the log export as part of the deliverables.

3) On-prem: we do offer a one-off on-prem (air-gapped) evaluation package — Laura will follow up with the options and an estimated SOW. If you want an on-prem run, turnaround is typically 3–4 weeks to provision and validate.

Shared assets: the clinician scorer Google Sheet is in the Drive folder above; I’ve added read access for your team (redwood-eval@redwood.ai has comment rights to populate example rows).

Next steps:
- Friday: CareBridge confirms upload method (SFTP or Drive) + selects retention window.
- Once upload completes: Redwood validates format (24 hrs) and schedules the run.
- Laura will send the onboarding SOW options if you want on-prem or extended audit SLA.

Ben and I will follow up with a short MOU + an eval quote (one-off). Appreciate the speed here — we’ll aim to get you first-pass results by next Tue if the sample lands on schedule.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales (Model Fit)
Redwood Inference
